 Preventing drowning among children during the rainy season.
 Drowning is one of the life-threatening risks for children, especially during the rainy season when river, stream, and lake water levels rise, currents are strong, and many areas pose potential dangers. Besides equipping children with swimming skills and water safety skills, preventing drowning requires regular coordination between schools, families, and local authorities to proactively protect children from unforeseen situations.
 Báo Đại Đoàn Kết • 09/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Proactively equip yourself with skills to prevent drowning accidents. 
 Drowning continues to be one of the leading causes of accidental death and injury among children in Vietnam.
 According to information released by the World Health Organization (WHO) on World Drowning Day, July 25, 2026, Vietnam is expected to record over 1,500 child deaths due to drowning in 2025, equivalent to an average of about 5 children per day. Although the number of deaths has decreased by more than 20% between 2020 and 2025, this situation still highlights the urgent need to continue implementing effective prevention measures. 
 The risk of drowning in children tends to increase during the summer months, when students are on vacation, have more time to play and participate in water activities. Especially during the rainy season, flooding creates many potentially dangerous areas such as waterholes, drainage ditches, manholes that are submerged or have strong currents, adding to the unpredictable risk of drowning accidents.
 Meanwhile, in rural areas, where there is a dense network of ponds, lakes, rivers, streams, canals, and ditches, children are frequently exposed to water environments, but not all of them are equipped with sufficient knowledge and skills to protect themselves.
 In light of this situation, many schools in Hanoi have proactively implemented comprehensive solutions to prevent drowning, considering it a crucial task in education and ensuring student safety.
 The activities went beyond mere propaganda and reminders, gradually becoming more concrete through life skills education programs, extracurricular activities, practical exercises, and collaboration with specialized units to organize swimming lessons.
 You may also like It is necessary to create a safe environment for children to prevent drowning. 
 Notably, many schools have collaborated with qualified sports centers and swimming pools to organize swimming lessons for students. The training content focuses not only on basic swimming techniques but also emphasizes water survival skills, such as how to float in emergencies, stay calm during cramps, recognize dangerous situations, and call for help when needed.
 Bringing water safety skills closer to students helps them proactively identify risks, develop reflexes to handle situations, and enhance their self-protection abilities. This is also a practical approach, shifting from mere propaganda to education through experience and practice.
 Not only schools, but also local authorities in many areas have actively coordinated the implementation of drowning prevention activities. According to a representative from the Culture and Social Affairs Department of Hoai Duc commune, in recent years, especially during the summer, drowning prevention has become a task that the locality pays attention to and directs the regular implementation of. Local authorities and schools must recognize this as an important content in the comprehensive education of students.
 A representative from the Hoai Duc Commune Department of Culture and Social Affairs emphasized: "Drowning prevention cannot be just a slogan; it must become a concrete, regular, and responsible action by the entire system. Schools, families, and the government must all work together, with safe swimming skills being a fundamental and long-term solution to minimize risks for children."
 Shift from reactive to proactive prevention. 
 Not only in Hanoi , but in recent years, drowning prevention efforts in schools across the country have seen positive changes. However, to achieve sustainable effectiveness, expanding the safe swimming instruction model needs to be implemented in parallel with education on prevention skills and raising awareness among families and communities in supervising children.
 Among various types of injuries, drowning is particularly dangerous because the incident can unfold very quickly, while the chances of saving a victim depend heavily on timely detection and intervention. It's important to note that knowing how to swim doesn't guarantee a child's safety in all situations. Factors such as strong currents, deep water, adverse weather, cramps, or panic can all put children at risk.
 Therefore, in addition to teaching swimming, students need to be equipped with knowledge to identify dangerous areas, the principle of not swimming or bathing in rivers, lakes, ponds, or streams without adult supervision; not playing near water edges, water containers, and places with danger warning signs. When they see someone drowning, children need to know how to shout for help, call adults and rescue forces, and not jump into the water to save someone without the appropriate skills and protective equipment.
 You may also like This orientation is also emphasized in Prime Minister's Directive No. 40/CD-TTg dated May 19, 2026, on strengthening the prevention and control of drowning among children. Accordingly, the Ministry of Education and Training is tasked with promoting education on knowledge and skills for preventing and controlling drowning; developing a movement to teach safe swimming, guiding safety skills in aquatic environments, and strengthening coordination between schools and families, especially during the summer break.
 This is an important basis for the education sector and localities to further concretize responsibilities in the work of protecting students. Depending on the actual conditions, educational institutions need to develop communication content suitable to the characteristics of the area, especially in areas with many rivers, lakes, ponds, canals, ditches or areas that frequently experience flooding.
 It is clear that preventing child drowning is not a temporary task, only addressed during the summer or when accidents occur, but rather a regular activity in every school, family, and community. From safe swimming lessons and life skills education sessions to fencing off ponds and lakes and warning about dangerous areas, every practical action contributes to protecting children from preventable risks. 
 Minh Long
